Thank you all for these critical findings. Let me summarize the three issues and assign actions before we close this meeting.

First, Daniel's title issue: the missing inventor assignment for the continuation application must be obtained and recorded before signing. Daniel, please circulate your title memorandum immediately after this meeting and coordinate with Northlake's tech transfer office to secure the missing assignment. If it cannot be obtained by Monday, we will need to either delay signing or carve that application out of the licensed patent rights.

Second, Sofia's royalty issue: the 3% running royalty exceeds the validated 225-basis-point market ceiling by 75 basis points. Sofia, please add the benchmark to the deal summary today. I will raise this with the business team — we either renegotiate down to or below 225 basis points before Monday, or document a written business rationale for the premium and include it in the approval package.

Third, Nora's export-controls issue: ECCN 3A001 classification requires military end-user prohibitions and annual end-use screening certifications. Nora, please add the classification to the transaction checklist today and draft the export-control provisions for insertion into the license agreement. I will coordinate with Northlake to accept these provisions before Monday.

All three issues must be resolved or documented in the approval package before signature. I am now formalizing the approval package with these remediation actions assigned. This meeting is closed.

Excellent points from all of you on these intersections. Let me address each briefly before we finalize.

Martin, I agree the carveout must be narrowly tailored to match exactly what Northlake's archived grant register describes — academic research and teaching uses only, nothing broader. Please flag any ambiguities in the prior grant's scope when you circulate the details, and Sofia's point is well taken: if the scope is ambiguous enough to create commercial exposure, that directly affects whether the 75-basis-point royalty premium can be justified.

Daniel, the intersection you've identified between the title remediation and the URC carveout is critical. If the continuation application gets carved out due to the missing assignment, the carveout language must not reference patent rights we don't hold. Please coordinate with Martin so the two drafting tracks are reconciled.

Nora, your point about deemed exports is an important catch. If the URC's academic research rights permit foreign national access to ECCN 3A001 technology, that's a deemed export risk. The carveout and the export-control provisions must be consistent — the military end-user prohibition and end-use screening requirements should apply to the consortium's preserved activities as well. Please coordinate with Martin so the carveout language and the export-control clauses are mutually reinforcing.

Sofia, please track the commercial-exposure question from Martin's carveout review as a potential input to the royalty justification analysis.

To be clear, these are refinements to the four action items already assigned — not new issues. Each of you has your assignment. Please execute and coordinate on the intersections we've just identified. I am formalizing the approval package now with these four remediation actions and their noted intersections. This meeting is closed.
